item.title: Vert.x - reactive applications on the JVM
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Vert.x - reactive applications on the JVM
Eclipse Vert.x is a toolkit, not a framework, for event-driven, non-blocking applications on the JVM. In 2016 (version 3.3.0) it could be used from Java, JavaScript, Groovy, Ruby and Ceylon; today (5.2.3) its examples are in Java and Kotlin.
https://vertx.io/1
Code: https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x
Vert.x is a tool-kit for building reactive applications on the JVM.

In 2016

Archived copy (2016-07-02): http://web.archive.org/web/20160702062634/http://vertx.io:80/

Vert.x is event driven and non blocking. This means your app can handle a lot of concurrency using a small number of kernel threads. Vert.x lets your app scale with minimal hardware.

Vert.x is not an application server. There’s no monolithic Vert.x instance into which you deploy applications. You just run your apps wherever you want to.
